name: Moab
source_summary: Son born to Lot through his older daughter after the destruction of Sodom, conceived when Lot's daughters made him drunk and slept with him out of fear their family line would otherwise end; became the ancestor of the Moabite people.
family_friendly_summary: Moab was born to Lot after his family escaped the destruction of the city of Sodom. Lot's wife had been lost, and his daughters, afraid there were no other men left to marry, made a very wrong and troubling decision that led to their father becoming Moab's father in a way the Bible does not hide or excuse. The Bible tells this part of the story honestly, even though it's a hard one, because Scripture doesn't pretend its people were perfect. Moab grew up to become the father of a whole nation, the Moabites, who lived east of the Dead Sea and interacted with Israel many times throughout the Old Testament, sometimes as enemies and sometimes, as in the story of Ruth, in more surprising and hopeful ways.
adult_story: Moab's origin is recorded in one of the more difficult passages of Genesis. After the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Lot and his two daughters took refuge in a cave in the hill country, having lost Lot's wife on the way (Genesis 19:26, 30). Believing there were no other men left to give them children -- an assumption Scripture does not confirm as accurate, since Zoar, a nearby town, had just been spared at their own request (19:20-22) -- the daughters made a plan: on successive nights they gave their father wine and slept with him while he was too intoxicated to be aware, each conceiving a son (19:31-36). Scripture states this plainly, without excusing Lot's drunkenness or his daughters' scheme, consistent with its wider pattern of recording its characters' sins honestly rather than hiding them. The older daughter named her son Moab -- an etymology traditionally understood to mean 'from father,' openly memorializing the shameful circumstance of his conception (19:37). Moab grew to become 'the father of the Moabites to this day,' a nation that settled east of the Dead Sea and figures repeatedly in Israel's later history -- sometimes as an antagonist, as in Balak's attempt to curse Israel through Balaam (Numbers 22-24) and Israel's later sin with Moabite women at Baal-peor (Numbers 25:1), and sometimes surprisingly, as the homeland of Ruth, a Moabite woman who became an ancestor of King David and, through him, of Christ (Ruth 1:4; 4:17; Matthew 1:5).
christ_connections: That a Moabite woman, Ruth, descended from this shameful origin, became an ancestress of Christ Himself (Matthew 1:5) shows that no family's beginnings, however dark, are beyond the reach of God's redemptive purpose.
